title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 1: Governance — Chapter Summary
intro: When many people live together they cannot all decide everything alone. Roads must be built, schools run, water supplied, forests protected. The art of taking such common decisions fairly and peacefully is GOVERNANCE. The form of governance where the PEOPLE themselves are the rulers is called DEMOCRACY. India is the world's largest democracy. This chapter explains what governance is, what makes a democracy, how India is organised into Union, State and Local levels, why the local level matters most for everyday life, and what it means to be an active citizen.

branches.label: Local self-government & citizenship

sections.heading: What is Governance?
bullets: Governance = the way a community organises itself to take decisions and get things done.
From a Greek root meaning 'to steer'.
Three pillars of GOOD governance: clear RULES, fair PROCESSES, and ACCOUNTABILITY.
Governance happens at many scales — family, school, village, country.
Three big questions of governance: WHO rules? HOW are decisions made? HOW is power limited?

sections.heading: What is Democracy?
bullets: Democracy = government by the PEOPLE (Greek: demos + kratos).
Most modern democracies, including India, are REPRESENTATIVE — the people elect representatives.
Every adult citizen has ONE vote of equal value.
Different parties and candidates can compete; no single party is forced.
Rulers' power is LIMITED by a Constitution and by laws.
Citizens have RIGHTS that the ruler cannot take away.

sections.heading: India as a Democratic Republic
bullets: India became independent on 15 August 1947.
The Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950 — Republic Day.
Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.
India is a SOVEREIGN, SOCIALIST, SECULAR, DEMOCRATIC, REPUBLIC.
Sovereign = independent; Secular = no official religion; Republic = elected head of state.
India is the world's LARGEST democracy by number of voters.

sections.heading: Three Levels of Government
bullets: UNION government — national subjects: defence, foreign affairs, currency, railways, post.
STATE government — state subjects: police, agriculture, public health, much of education.
LOCAL government — village wells, street lights, school maintenance, local sanitation.
Rural local government = PANCHAYATI RAJ.
Urban local government = Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council or Nagar Panchayat.

sections.heading: Why Local Government Matters
bullets: Local government is closest to people — it lives with the local problem.
Mahatma Gandhi championed GRAM SWARAJ — village self-rule.
The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments (1992) gave a constitutional foundation to Panchayats and Municipalities.
These amendments require regular elections, reserve seats for women / SCs / STs, and give local bodies clear powers.
They turned local government from an idea into a working reality across India.

sections.heading: Rights, Duties and Participation
bullets: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS include the right to equality, freedom of speech, freedom of religion, fair laws.
FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES include respecting the Constitution and the flag, protecting public property, safeguarding the environment.
A citizen aged 18 can VOTE in elections.
Citizens can stand for election, contact representatives, attend gram-sabha / ward meetings, and use RTI.
Children too can practise democracy — through school councils and family discussions.

sections.heading: Governance Beyond Elections
bullets: Voting once every five years is necessary but not sufficient.
A FREE PRESS can criticise the government without fear.
An INDEPENDENT JUDICIARY can strike down bad laws.
STRONG INSTITUTIONS — Election Commission, CAG, public service commissions — hold the government accountable.
ACTIVE CIVIL SOCIETY — NGOs, citizens' groups, gram sabhas — keeps governance honest between elections.

key_takeaways: Governance = how a community decides and acts together; needs rules, fair processes, accountability.
Democracy = rule by the people; in modern democracies through elected representatives.
India became independent on 15 Aug 1947 and a Republic on 26 Jan 1950.
India is Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic; world's largest democracy.
Three levels of government: Union, State, Local.
Local government — Panchayati Raj (rural) and Municipalities (urban) — is closest to the people; 73rd & 74th Amendments (1992) gave it constitutional backing.
Citizens have RIGHTS and DUTIES; participation is the heart of democracy.
Free press, independent courts, strong institutions and civil society keep governance honest between elections.

glossary.definition: The way a community organises itself to take decisions and get things done fairly.
A form of government in which the people themselves are the rulers, usually through elected representatives.
The supreme written law of a country that lays down how the government works and the rights of citizens.
Independent; no foreign country can decide what the country must do.
Treating all religions equally; the state itself has no official religion.
A state in which the head of state is elected, not a hereditary king or queen.
The central government of India, dealing with national subjects like defence and foreign affairs.
The government of a state or Union Territory with a legislature, dealing with state subjects.
Government at the village (Panchayati Raj) or city (Municipality) level, closest to the people.
The system of rural local self-government in India, organised around village panchayats.
Village self-rule; the principle, championed by Gandhi, that strong villages make a strong India.
The 1992 amendment giving constitutional status, regular elections and reserved seats to rural Panchayats.
The 1992 amendment giving constitutional status to urban Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats.
Rights guaranteed by the Constitution, such as equality, free speech, and freedom of religion.
Duties listed in the Constitution that every citizen is expected to follow.
